plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU) to eliminate that risk.
Sell SMH to reduce semiconductor exposure.
Trim QQQI to 20% to reduce concentration and favor income.

conservative.read: This mode targets approximately 1.5% per month by focusing on capital preservation. It significantly reduces leverage and concentrates on income and broad market exposure, aiming for low drawdowns.

plan: Trim leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU) to a small percentage.
Trim QQQI to 25% to reduce concentration while retaining income exposure.
Trim SMH to 5% to reduce semiconductor exposure.
Buy ZS as a new quality tech position.

This plan balances risk reduction with growth opportunities.
balanced.read: This mode targets approximately 2.5% per month with a risk-first growth approach. It reduces leverage and concentration while adding quality names and diversification, maintaining a moderate cash buffer.

plan: Trim QQQI to 20% to reduce concentration and reallocate to higher conviction areas.
Trim SMH to 5% to reduce semiconductor exposure.
Add to leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU) to increase exposure.
Buy ZS as a new high-conviction tech position.
Buy XLF to add diversification and potential growth.
This plan aggressively pursues growth by increasing leverage and concentration in strong setups.
aggressive.read: This mode targets approximately 4% per month, aiming for stretched growth. It increases leverage and concentration in high-scoring setups, accepting higher potential upside and significantly larger drawdowns. Leveraged ETF decay is a key risk.

plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU) to remove volatility.
Sell SMH and CRWD to exit high-beta tech and semiconductor exposure.
Add to QQQI to increase focus on income generation.
Add to SPY to capture broad market exposure for potential income.

It aims for low drawdowns by minimizing speculative positions.
income.read: This mode targets approximately 1% per month, focusing on parking cash for yield. It prioritizes income-generating assets and broad index exposure, cutting leverage and high-beta single names to near zero. NAV can still fall in market downturns.
